core_obligations: Statement (lines 1655-1661): with notation and hypotheses of the morphism-of-simplicial-sites lemma, for K in D(O) one has (g'_n)^* Rh_{total,*} K = Rh_{n,*} g_n^* K.

Exactness setup (proof lines 1663-1668): g_n^* = g_n^{-1} because g_n^{-1}O = O_n (by the restriction construction); hence g_n^* is exact and Lg_n^* is given by applying g_n^* to any representative, likewise for g'_n.

Reduction (lines 1668-1679): there is a canonical base change map (Cohomology on Sites remark); by the modules-abelian-unbounded lemma its image in D(C'_n) is the map (g'_n)^{-1}Rh_{total,*}K_ab -> Rh_{n,*}g_n^{-1}K_ab, which is an isomorphism by the abelian-case lemma; the result follows.
proof_roadmap: Note g_n^* = g_n^{-1} (ring restriction) so derived pullback is plain pullback on representatives.
Take the canonical base change map and identify it with the abelian-case map.
Conclude by the proven abelian isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: Base-change lemma for modules (statement 1655-1661, proof 1663-1679): the ringed-site base change isomorphism - the proof notes g_n^* = g_n^{-1} with the exactness consequences, forms the canonical base change map, and identifies it in the derived category with the abelian-case map via the modules-abelian-unbounded lemma, transferring the already-proven abelian isomorphism; the reduction is executed in-span. H2.
